lines.text: Mirelle's letter was nine lines of numbers. Page, line and word. Anyone could have read it, if they had read past page one of the Charter.
It took me two hours and every candle in the hall. Tamsin checked my sums. She trusts nobody's sums but her own.
Lord Lucan. My uncle is ill, and has not left his bed in a month. His physicians are Order physicians. I may not see him.
The Grand Measurer speaks for the King now. He signs for him. Some days I think he breathes for him.
King Edric was sick, and Vance ruled. Not from the throne. From beside it, which is safer.
Your father is alive. He is under the cathedral, in the deep vault, near where you found the girl.
The guards say he doesn't speak. He sits all day with his back against the wall, listening. They say someone hums, on the other side of it.
I read that line four times. Then I went out into the snow, and stood there until Bram came to find me.
What is it, my lord?
They've put my father next to her. The woman under the cathedral. He sits against the wall, listening to her hum.
Bram said nothing. But his face went as white as it had the night I first hummed that song to my wards. I didn't understand it then.
Midwinter, at noon, in the Square of the Seven. Vance wants the whole city to watch. At dawn that day, I will open the river door. After that, nothing.
Prince Aurelio of Calvere has extended his visit. He dines with the Grand Measurer every night. I don't like it.
And tell your archer she still drops her left shoulder.
I do not.
She did, a little. Nobody told her.
That night the council fought about who would go. I wanted to go. Everyone else wanted me not to.
You're the most wanted man in Aldmere, and you can't lift a sword. Walk into that square, and Vance gets two Varrs for the price of one.
She was right. I hated that she was right. I hated it all night.
In the end there were four. Wren, for the arrow. Oswin, for the sword. Tamsin, who knew the Order's codes. And Ilse, who knew its Measurers.
We'll bring him home, my lord. I got my sister out of that place. I can get your father out.
Before they could leave, a rider came to the gate alone, on a tired grey horse, in a long navy coat with a silver lens on a chain.
Magister Silas Hask had come to Greyhollow again. This time, he had come to stay.
The Lord Who Measured Zero. Chapter one hundred and twenty-seven, coming soon.
